x: On the 19th November we had Woodford Green A.C. and the Royal Military Police (Woking) as visitors to Belgrave Hall, for an 8 aside match over our 5 miles cross-country course. Bromley of the Police was first man home just in front of Vern Blowfield and Jack Brown.
Vern Blowfield had an easy run in fourth position and it looks as if these three will form the spearhead of our team for the coming cross-country championships.
At the end of the first lap Vern Blowfield and Derrick Burfitt were running stride for stride in the lead followed by Les Stokell and Jack Brown.
Derrick Burfitt was second in this race last year, but this time could not get nearer than eighth with Vern Blowfield ninth. As the first seven home included such runners as Alec Olney, D.
When they came in sight again Jack Brown was out in front followed by Charlton, who was running in borrowed rubbers, then came Bill Lucas and the holder Vern Blowfield came in fourth.

Vern Blowfield after making a fast start had a bad time and fell right back but came through again later on to finish in the first 100. Ted Stimpson ran his usual dependable race and Steve Charlton also did well as did Stan Davies, our new Track Captain, and with four in the first 33 we should have…

The Senior race saw the huge field of 493 runners and the leading positions never changed after the first lap and it was quite refreshing to see a bunch of four Southern runners behind Aaron, the winner, and it was a pity that Vern Blowfield was not among them as many think he could have been if he had run.
The individual race was won by Vern Blowfield, who ran in quite his old style to win by half-a-minute from Bill Lucas, our 1948 Olympic Games representative.

…ll-known runners who have done this stage and yet not come within a minute of Olney's time, well all we can say is that Vern Blowfield was not disgraced in handing over in 9th position and his time was actually faster than Derrick Burfitt did over the same leg last year.…
In the 1 mile it was our turn to score a “ maximum ” and we actually had the first three men home, with Jack Brown leading Vern Blowfield and Ches Walker in the good time of 4 min. 31.4 secs.

Vern Blowfield did 4.31, running first, then Jack Brown 4.34, Bill Lucas 4.46, and Derrick Burfitt 4.34 to come home winners. In the 3 miles Team Race we had Jack Bragginton, George Lucas, Steve Charlton and Len Bishop, but could only manage a 4th place in this event.

Harry Churcher once again won the Business Houses 2 Miles Track Championship, with Bob McMullen 2nd and at the same meeting young Dan Godfrey won the 100 and 200 Youths' events. Vern Blowfield won the 1 mile title when beating Stan Cox, the Olympic Games runner.
The 3 miles saw Vern Blowfield, Bill Lucas, Len Herbert and Charlie Smart running in our colours and at one stage of the race the Belgrave vests were in the two leading positions.

Derrick Burfitt and Ches Walker were first and second in the 880 yards, and Bill Lucas won the 1 mile with Vern Blowfield in third place. Len Herbert won the 2 miles race in 9 min. 34.4 secs., but we were beaten in the team race by S.L.H.
Vern Blowfield won the 1 mile match and also finished third in the open mile handicap which was won by Bill Lucas with Bob Taylor second, did I hear someone say what a Handicapper?
We thus led throughout and with Len Herbert, Derrick Burfitt, Vern Blowfield and Jack Brown to call on, it is a pity that the “ National ” Brighton Relay has been put off until April, 1951.
In the 3 Miles championship, the holder, Vern Blowfield, was not defending and with Bill Lucas and Len Herbert also absent, the race was a very open one.

Bill Lucas came next and he was followed by Jack Brown, Vern Blowfield and Ches Walker, who came in together, with Bob Taylor and Ted Stimpson close behind, and this laid the foundation of our win in the team race over our old and friendly rivals.
Vern Blowfield was our next runner, and behind him were Woodford Green, Essex Beagles and Aylesford, battling together, and the latter two clubs were represented by J.

In both events Belgrave were well to the fore, as in the senior event Ted Stimpson, Bill Lucas, Archie Bedford, Vern Blowfield, Eric Herbert, Jack Bragginton and Steve Charlton were well up, and Ray Tooby and Bob Taylor were in the lead in the junior race.
Among these were Vern Blowfield and Les Stokell, while Archie Bedford also stated his intention to do only one lap but then evidently changed his mind and ran well to finish in 4th position.
Vern Blowfield also took this opportunity to have a run out with the lads and we hope that next season we shall see him once again doing his “stuff” over the country.

Abbott, both London University runners, followed by Len Bishop and Colin Collis, yet another London member, with Ray Tooby just in front of three ex-International runners in Vern Blowfield, Ted Stimpson and Tom Carter.

Eric Bishop kept this position on the next stage and then Eddie Short lost one more place to Jim Peters of Essex Beagles and although Bill Lucas took us back into 3rd position our final runner Vern Blowfield found he could not make any impression on Jimmy Wood and Tommy Rowe who were in front of him.

Vern Blowfield showed a welcome return in finishing 12th with Len Adams 18th, Ken Stimpson 31st, Ted Stimpson 36th, Len Bishop 37th, Eric Bishop 40th, Doug Briggs 45th, Alan Bishop 48th, George Stace 49th, Steve Charlton 51st, Bob Taylor 52nd, A.

We were pleased to see Vern Blowfield once more appearing in our colours, and although he seemed rather short of training we are sure he will soon get back to the form which gained him second place in the English cross-country championship in 1948 at Sheffield.

Archie Bedford finished third in the individual race with Vern Blowfield in fifth place, and then came Jimmy Wood 13th with Len Bishop 16th, and the latter just beat Tom Richards, the well known marathon runner.
Vern Blowfield was 25th, Tony Snoad 26th, Bob Taylor 37th, Ken Stimpson 50th and Ted Stimpson 53rd. Others to finish were—Steve Charlton 54th, J.
Next came Vern Blowfield, making a welcome re-appearance together with Eddie Short who was finding the going a bit too hard for him, as I think he prefers more muddy conditions.

Our lads were running well together but seemed too far back although Vern Blowfield was going great guns and Eddie Short was also well up. On the second lap we saw Charlie Walker, Eddie Short, Jack Brown and Archie Bedford running well together with Bill Lucas, our captain, acting as the whipper-in.

It was very pleasing to see Vern Blowfield once more leading our team home and gaining for himself the "Harry Parker" Memorial Trophy, and a replica of the "Finch-Wayte Cup" for being the first scoring member of the first Southern club to finish in this championship.
Bill Lucas then took us to the front on the third stage but Vern Blowfield could not hold Alec Olney over the final "leg," and so we finished 2nd to Thames Valley H.
Butler were second and third in the 220, and we also won the 2 miles team race, with Vern Blowfield leading the field home and scored yet another win in the 1 mile medley relay.

Vern Blowfield and "Ginger" Newell also gained standards in the 1 mile and we have quite a number of milers now doing inside 4.25 which goes to show how much the standard within the Club has improved in recent years.

Bob Taylor won the 880 yards while Holtum was second in the 100 yards, and Vern Blowfield won the 3 miles run in 15 min. 4 secs. Ian Badiali was second in the 440 but we were short of competitors for the two field events which were included in the match.
We were pleased to see Vern Blowfield win the 2 miles run and his time of 9 min. 42.6 secs. was good, seeing that he had to slow down over the last 100 yards owing to Achilles’ tendon trouble.

Vern Blowfield also writes to say that his family are now with him at Oxford, but that he hopes to come up for some training runs and says he is looking forward to having a good season and takes it as a good omen that the Southern is at Aylesford, as in 1948 at the same venue he was 3rd in the indiv…
Notable absentees included previous winners in Vern Blowfield and Len Herbert, and we had Eric Herbert running in the Civil Service race on the same day.
The Middlesex event was held at Trent Park and here again Cadogan A.C. were weakened by the absence of Vern Blowfield, Tony Snoad, "Ginger" Newell and J.
Vern Blowfield hands the baton over to Ted who sets off on the second leg of the "News of the World" London to Brighton Relay held on April 19th 1947.

Our expectancies rose again with our win in the Southern Championships at Hadleigh where we beat Aylesford Paper Mills by 10 points with our six scoring men in 43 places led by a good solo performance in 11th spot by Vern Blowfield.
On the first small lap of the senior race Vern Blowfield was up to the front with Aaron, the eventual winner, but could not hold his position and gradually fell back.
